Close side: the row's final verse, MT 15:8, ends the applied sentence against Jerusalem's inhabitants and carries the utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature at its own end, matched by a pe mark recorded on 15:8 in the single-witness paragraph layer. A samekh mark sits earlier, on 15:5 (sweep: 8 verses), where the riddle's own question -- whether the vine-wood, even charred, is fit for any use -- reaches its rhetorical dead end before the messenger formula כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.15.6) opens the application at 15:6. That mid-chapter mark is weighed and not adopted as the row seam: the application (15:6-8) answers the riddle (15:1-5) rather than opening an independent formula-bounded unit of its own, and a three-verse application row would not itself carry a fresh word-event onset. The row is therefore kept as the whole chapter, with the internal mark disclosed rather than acted on.
